title: Cemetery fees review and Fergus main street lighting
subtitle: Belsyde Cemetery expansion, urban forestry, Business Park sale terms, Letter of Credit Policy, Storybrook road agreement, OPP report.
overview: Council approved most of a consultant's cemetery products, services and fees review, but excluded several recommendations, including the proposed increases to infant and child burial fees. New rates will go into the 2025 Rates and Fees By-law during budget deliberations. Council also received an update on the Belsyde Cemetery Block D expansion, where in-ground burial lots are nearly used up.

Council authorized staff to carry out My Main Street grant projects in Fergus: night markets, more Twilight in Templin events and pilot lighting of heritage buildings. The grant has a tight year-end completion deadline, and staff were directed to explore a second lighting phase.

Council changed the standard Business Park land sale agreement, endorsed a Letter of Credit Policy and approved an early payment agreement with the Storybrook developers for realigning and urbanizing Colborne Street. It also confirmed its intention to designate 6550 Gerrie Road, Elora, as a heritage property. Council heard the OPP's 2023 report and received the urban forestry update. Nothing came forward from closed session.
Council extended the meeting curfew to complete its agenda.

decisions.detail: Council approved the consultant's recommendations except 6 (a), (g), (h), (k) and 7, and directed staff to put the new rates and fees in the 2025 Rates and Fees By-law {{vote:m5}}.
Council delegated authority to sign the FedDev Ontario funding agreement and select buildings for pilot lighting in Fergus, and directed staff to explore a second lighting phase {{vote:m8}}.
The CAO may use the revised standard agreement of purchase and sale for Business Park land sales, effective immediately {{vote:m9}}.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign a by-law endorsing the Letter of Credit Policy {{vote:m10}}.
Council authorized an early payment agreement with the Storybrook developers for off-site works, including the Colborne Street reconstruction {{vote:m11}}.
Through the consent agenda, Council confirmed its intention to designate 6550 Gerrie Road, Elora, as a property of cultural heritage value or interest {{vote:m3}}.
Council passed by-laws 2024-69 to 2024-72: an Ontario Lottery and Gaming funding policy, the Storybrook financing agreement, the Letter of Credit Policy and the Gerrie Road designation {{vote:m12}}.

debate: On cemetery fees, a councillor proposed keeping infant and child burial fees unchanged instead of raising them. Staff said the effect on the budget would be small, though holding fees static could mean some tax subsidy as costs rise.
The consultants said the fee review aims to align with regional neighbours, not to make cemeteries revenue neutral. Moving to a break-even model would need further analysis.

Councillors asked how higher fees affect residents who have prepaid and how a non-resident premium would treat seniors who moved to care homes. Consultants said residency can be defined in the by-law, and staff noted that the premium was only to be studied over three years.

On the Fergus lighting project, councillors asked about energy-efficient LED lighting and building owner support. Staff said owners had been positive but pricing was still pending, with supplier delivery of two to 16 weeks against a year-end deadline.

On Storybrook, councillors asked about sidewalks, parking and emergency access. Staff said sidewalks would be on both sides, there would be no driveways onto the road, and the realignment should not slow access to the hospital.
